title: The hidden fires of the Flame Nebula
caption: The Flame Nebula and surroundings, imaged by ESO's VISTA survey telescope
celestial: Flame Nebula, NGC 2024 · constellation Orion · about 1500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESO/J. Emerson/VISTA. Acknowledgment: Cambridge Astronomical Survey Unit

recognition.text: Ranked #19 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A star-forming cloud glows in this wide infrared view, with the reflection nebula NGC 2023 just below centre, the faint outline of the Horsehead Nebula towards the lower right, and a bright bluish star to the right. The main subject is the Flame Nebula, NGC 2024, in the constellation of Orion.

This was the first image released publicly from VISTA, described by ESO as the world's largest survey telescope. In visible light, thick dust completely hides the Flame's core. Infrared light slips through that dust, so the cluster of very young stars at the nebula's heart comes into view.

That is the great strength of infrared astronomy for studying star formation, because newborn stars usually sit deep inside the dusty clouds that formed them, where visible light cannot escape. That bright bluish star on the right belongs to the trio of bright stars forming Orion's Belt.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (42.92 x 52.52 arcminutes) and distance (1500 light years), the frame spans roughly 19 × 23 light-years. Its light set out about 1,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a near-infrared image from VISTA's VIRCAM camera, using J, H and Ks filters. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.

understand.eye: Infrared light is invisible to the eye, and by eye or in visible-light photos the Flame's core stays hidden behind dust.

explore: The picture was made from exposures through the J, H and Ks near-infrared filters, with a total exposure time of 14 minutes. It covers about half of VISTA's full field, roughly 40 by 50 arcminutes.
alt: A glowing nebula with a cluster of young stars at its core, a smaller glow below centre, a faint horsehead outline at lower right, and a bright bluish star at right.
